p.src: Enter two Clowns with spades, &c.
FIRST CLOWN. Is she to be buried in Christian burial, when she wilfully seeks her own salvation?

u.src: Is she to be buried in Christian burial, when she wilfully seeks her own salvation?

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. I tell thee she is, and therefore make her grave straight. The crowner hath sat on her, and finds it Christian burial.

u.src: I tell thee she is, and therefore make her grave straight.
The crowner hath sat on her, and finds it Christian burial.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. How can that be, unless she drowned herself in her own defence?

u.src: How can that be, unless she drowned herself in her own defence?

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Why, ’tis found so.

FIRST CLOWN. It must be se offendendo, it cannot be else. For here lies the point: if I drown myself wittingly, it argues an act: and an act hath three branches. It is to act, to do, and to perform: argal, she drowned herself wittingly.

u.src: It must be se offendendo, it cannot be else.
For here lies the point: if I drown myself wittingly, it argues an act: and an act hath three branches.
It is to act, to do, and to perform: argal, she drowned herself wittingly.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Nay, but hear you, goodman delver,—

u.src: Nay, but hear you, goodman delver,—

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Give me leave. Here lies the water; good. Here stands the man; good. If the man go to this water and drown himself, it is, will he nill he, he goes,—mark you that. But if the water come to him and drown him, he drowns not himself. Argal, he that is not guilty of his own death shortens not his own life.

u.src: If the man go to this water and drown himself, it is, will he nill he, he goes,—mark you that.
But if the water come to him and drown him, he drowns not himself.
Argal, he that is not guilty of his own death shortens not his own life.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. But is this law?
FIRST CLOWN. Ay, marry, is’t, crowner’s quest law.

u.src: Ay, marry, is’t, crowner’s quest law.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Will you ha’ the truth on’t? If this had not been a gentlewoman, she should have been buried out o’ Christian burial.

u.src: Will you ha’ the truth on’t?
If this had not been a gentlewoman, she should have been buried out o’ Christian burial.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Why, there thou say’st. And the more pity that great folk should have countenance in this world to drown or hang themselves more than their even Christian. Come, my spade. There is no ancient gentlemen but gardeners, ditchers, and grave-makers: they hold up Adam’s profession.

u.src: Why, there thou say’st. And the more pity that great folk should have countenance in this world to drown or hang themselves more than their even Christian.
There is no ancient gentlemen but gardeners, ditchers, and grave-makers: they hold up Adam’s profession.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Was he a gentleman?
FIRST CLOWN. He was the first that ever bore arms.

u.src: He was the first that ever bore arms.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Why, he had none.

FIRST CLOWN. What, art a heathen? How dost thou understand the Scripture? The Scripture says Adam digg’d. Could he dig without arms? I’ll put another question to thee. If thou answerest me not to the purpose, confess thyself—

u.src: How dost thou understand the Scripture?
I’ll put another question to thee.
If thou answerest me not to the purpose, confess thyself—

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Go to.
FIRST CLOWN. What is he that builds stronger than either the mason, the shipwright, or the carpenter?

u.src: What is he that builds stronger than either the mason, the shipwright, or the carpenter?

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. The gallows-maker; for that frame outlives a thousand tenants.

u.src: The gallows-maker; for that frame outlives a thousand tenants.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. I like thy wit well in good faith, the gallows does well. But how does it well? It does well to those that do ill. Now, thou dost ill to say the gallows is built stronger than the church; argal, the gallows may do well to thee. To’t again, come.

u.src: I like thy wit well in good faith, the gallows does well.
It does well to those that do ill.
Now, thou dost ill to say the gallows is built stronger than the church; argal, the gallows may do well to thee.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Who builds stronger than a mason, a shipwright, or a carpenter?

u.src: Who builds stronger than a mason, a shipwright, or a carpenter?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Ay, tell me that, and unyoke.

u.src: Ay, tell me that, and unyoke.

p.src: SECOND CLOWN. Marry, now I can tell.
FIRST CLOWN. To’t.
SECOND CLOWN. Mass, I cannot tell.
Enter Hamlet and Horatio, at a distance.

u.src: Enter Hamlet and Horatio, at a distance.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Cudgel thy brains no more about it, for your dull ass will not mend his pace with beating; and when you are asked this question next, say ‘a grave-maker’. The houses he makes last till doomsday. Go, get thee to Yaughan; fetch me a stoup of liquor.

u.src: Cudgel thy brains no more about it, for your dull ass will not mend his pace with beating; and when you are asked this question next, say ‘a grave-maker’.

Go, get thee to Yaughan; fetch me a stoup of liquor.

p.src: \[Exit Second Clown.\]
\[Digs and sings.\]
In youth when I did love, did love, Methought it was very sweet; To contract, O, the time for, a, my behove, O methought there was nothing meet.

u.src: In youth when I did love, did love, Methought it was very sweet; To contract, O, the time for, a, my behove, O methought there was nothing meet.

p.src: HAMLET. Has this fellow no feeling of his business, that he sings at grave-making?

u.src: Has this fellow no feeling of his business, that he sings at grave-making?

p.src: HORATIO. Custom hath made it in him a property of easiness.

u.src: Custom hath made it in him a property of easiness.

p.src: HAMLET. ’Tis e’en so; the hand of little employment hath the daintier sense.

u.src: ’Tis e’en so; the hand of little employment hath the daintier sense.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. \[Sings.\] But age with his stealing steps Hath claw’d me in his clutch, And hath shipp’d me into the land, As if I had never been such.

u.src: \[Sings.\] But age with his stealing steps Hath claw’d me in his clutch, And hath shipp’d me into the land, As if I had never been such.

p.src: \[Throws up a skull.\]

HAMLET. That skull had a tongue in it, and could sing once. How the knave jowls it to th’ ground, as if ’twere Cain’s jawbone, that did the first murder! This might be the pate of a politician which this ass now o’er-offices, one that would circumvent God, might it not?

u.src: That skull had a tongue in it, and could sing once.

This might be the pate of a politician which this ass now o’er-offices, one that would circumvent God, might it not?

p.src: HORATIO. It might, my lord.

HAMLET. Or of a courtier, which could say ‘Good morrow, sweet lord! How dost thou, good lord?’ This might be my lord such-a-one, that praised my lord such-a-one’s horse when he meant to beg it, might it not?

u.src: Or of a courtier, which could say ‘Good morrow, sweet lord!
This might be my lord such-a-one, that praised my lord such-a-one’s horse when he meant to beg it, might it not?

p.src: HORATIO. Ay, my lord.

HAMLET. Why, e’en so: and now my Lady Worm’s; chapless, and knocked about the mazard with a sexton’s spade. Here’s fine revolution, an we had the trick to see’t. Did these bones cost no more the breeding but to play at loggets with ’em? Mine ache to think on’t.

u.src: Why, e’en so: and now my Lady Worm’s; chapless, and knocked about the mazard with a sexton’s spade.
Here’s fine revolution, an we had the trick to see’t.
Did these bones cost no more the breeding but to play at loggets with ’em?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. \[Sings.\] A pickaxe and a spade, a spade, For and a shrouding-sheet; O, a pit of clay for to be made For such a guest is meet.

u.src: \[Sings.\] A pickaxe and a spade, a spade, For and a shrouding-sheet; O, a pit of clay for to be made For such a guest is meet.

p.src: \[Throws up another skull.\]

HAMLET. There’s another. Why may not that be the skull of a lawyer? Where be his quiddits now, his quillets, his cases, his tenures, and his tricks? Why does he suffer this rude knave now to knock him about the sconce with a dirty shovel, and will not tell him of his action of battery? Hum. This fellow might be in’s time a great buyer of land, with his statutes, his recognizances, his fines, his double vouchers, his recoveries. Is this the fine of his fines, and the recovery of his recoveries, to have his fine pate full of fine dirt? Will his vouchers vouch him no more of his purchases, and double ones too, than the length and breadth of a pair of indentures?

p.src: HAMLET. Is not parchment made of sheep-skins?

u.src: Is not parchment made of sheep-skins?

p.src: HORATIO. Ay, my lord, and of calf-skins too.

u.src: Ay, my lord, and of calf-skins too.

p.src: HAMLET. They are sheep and calves which seek out assurance in that. I will speak to this fellow.—Whose grave’s this, sir?

u.src: They are sheep and calves which seek out assurance in that.
I will speak to this fellow.—Whose grave’s this, sir?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Mine, sir. \[Sings.\] O, a pit of clay for to be made For such a guest is meet.

u.src: \[Sings.\] O, a pit of clay for to be made For such a guest is meet.

p.src: HAMLET. I think it be thine indeed, for thou liest in’t.

u.src: I think it be thine indeed, for thou liest in’t.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. You lie out on’t, sir, and therefore ’tis not yours. For my part, I do not lie in’t, yet it is mine.

u.src: You lie out on’t, sir, and therefore ’tis not yours.
For my part, I do not lie in’t, yet it is mine.

p.src: HAMLET. Thou dost lie in’t, to be in’t and say it is thine. ’Tis for the dead, not for the quick; therefore thou liest.

u.src: Thou dost lie in’t, to be in’t and say it is thine.
’Tis for the dead, not for the quick; therefore thou liest.

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. ’Tis a quick lie, sir; ’t will away again from me to you.

u.src: ’Tis a quick lie, sir; ’t will away again from me to you.

p.src: HAMLET. What man dost thou dig it for?

u.src: What man dost thou dig it for?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. For no man, sir.
HAMLET. What woman then?
FIRST CLOWN. For none neither.
HAMLET. Who is to be buried in’t?

u.src: Who is to be buried in’t?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. One that was a woman, sir; but, rest her soul, she’s dead.

u.src: One that was a woman, sir; but, rest her soul, she’s dead.

p.src: HAMLET. How absolute the knave is! We must speak by the card, or equivocation will undo us. By the Lord, Horatio, these three years I have taken note of it, the age is grown so picked that the toe of the peasant comes so near the heel of the courtier he galls his kibe.—How long hast thou been a grave-maker?

u.src: We must speak by the card, or equivocation will undo us.

By the Lord, Horatio, these three years I have taken note of it, the age is grown so picked that the toe of the peasant comes so near the heel of the courtier he galls his kibe.—How long hast thou been a grave-maker?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Of all the days i’ th’ year, I came to’t that day that our last King Hamlet o’ercame Fortinbras.

u.src: Of all the days i’ th’ year, I came to’t that day that our last King Hamlet o’ercame Fortinbras.

p.src: HAMLET. How long is that since?
FIRST CLOWN. Cannot you tell that? Every fool can tell that. It was the very day that young Hamlet was born,—he that is mad, and sent into England.

u.src: It was the very day that young Hamlet was born,—he that is mad, and sent into England.

p.src: HAMLET. Ay, marry, why was he sent into England?

u.src: Ay, marry, why was he sent into England?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Why, because he was mad; he shall recover his wits there; or if he do not, it’s no great matter there.

u.src: Why, because he was mad; he shall recover his wits there; or if he do not, it’s no great matter there.

p.src: HAMLET. Why?
FIRST CLOWN. ’Twill not be seen in him there; there the men are as mad as he.

u.src: ’Twill not be seen in him there; there the men are as mad as he.

p.src: HAMLET. How came he mad?
FIRST CLOWN. Very strangely, they say.
HAMLET. How strangely?
FIRST CLOWN. Faith, e’en with losing his wits.

u.src: Faith, e’en with losing his wits.

p.src: HAMLET. Upon what ground?
FIRST CLOWN. Why, here in Denmark. I have been sexton here, man and boy, thirty years.

u.src: I have been sexton here, man and boy, thirty years.

p.src: HAMLET. How long will a man lie i’ th’earth ere he rot?

u.src: How long will a man lie i’ th’earth ere he rot?

p.src: FIRST CLOWN. Faith, if he be not rotten before he die,—as we have many pocky corses nowadays that will scarce hold the laying in,—he will last you some eight year or nine year. A tanner will last you nine year.

u.src: Faith, if he be not rotten before he die,—as we have many pocky corses nowadays that will scarce hold the laying in,—he will last you some eight year or nine year.
A tanner will last you nine year.

p.src: HAMLET. Why he more than another?

FIRST CLOWN. Why, sir, his hide is so tann’d with his trade that he will keep out water a great while. And your water is a sore decayer of your whoreson dead body. Here’s a skull now; this skull hath lain in the earth three-and-twenty years.

u.src: Why, sir, his hide is so tann’d with his trade that he will keep out water a great while.
And your water is a sore decayer of your whoreson dead body.
Here’s a skull now; this skull hath lain in the earth three-and-twenty years.

p.src: HAMLET. Whose was it?
FIRST CLOWN. A whoreson, mad fellow’s it was. Whose do you think it was?

u.src: A whoreson, mad fellow’s it was.
Whose do you think it was?

p.src: HAMLET. Nay, I know not.
FIRST CLOWN. A pestilence on him for a mad rogue! A pour’d a flagon of Rhenish on my head once. This same skull, sir, was Yorick’s skull, the King’s jester.

u.src: A pestilence on him for a mad rogue!
A pour’d a flagon of Rhenish on my head once.
This same skull, sir, was Yorick’s skull, the King’s jester.

p.src: HAMLET. This?
FIRST CLOWN. E’en that.

HAMLET. Let me see. \[Takes the skull.\] Alas, poor Yorick. I knew him, Horatio, a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy. He hath borne me on his back a thousand times; and now, how abhorred in my imagination it is! My gorge rises at it. Here hung those lips that I have kiss’d I know not how oft. Where be your gibes now? your gambols? your songs? your flashes of merriment, that were wont to set the table on a roar? Not one now, to mock your own grinning? Quite chop-fallen? Now get you to my lady’s chamber, and tell her, let her paint an inch thick, to this favour she must come. Make her laugh at that.—Prithee, Horatio, tell me one thing.

p.src: HORATIO. What’s that, my lord?
HAMLET. Dost thou think Alexander looked o’ this fashion i’ th’earth?

u.src: Dost thou think Alexander looked o’ this fashion i’ th’earth?

p.src: HORATIO. E’en so.
HAMLET. And smelt so? Pah!
\[Throws down the skull.\]
HORATIO. E’en so, my lord.
HAMLET. To what base uses we may return, Horatio! Why may not imagination trace the noble dust of Alexander till he find it stopping a bung-hole?

u.src: To what base uses we may return, Horatio!
Why may not imagination trace the noble dust of Alexander till he find it stopping a bung-hole?

p.src: HORATIO. ’Twere to consider too curiously to consider so.

u.src: ’Twere to consider too curiously to consider so.

p.src: HAMLET. No, faith, not a jot. But to follow him thither with modesty enough, and likelihood to lead it; as thus. Alexander died, Alexander was buried, Alexander returneth into dust; the dust is earth; of earth we make loam; and why of that loam whereto he was converted might they not stop a beer-barrel? Imperious Caesar, dead and turn’d to clay, Might stop a hole to keep the wind away. O, that that earth which kept the world in awe Should patch a wall t’expel the winter’s flaw. But soft! but soft! aside! Here comes the King.

p.src: The Queen, the courtiers. Who is that they follow? And with such maimed rites? This doth betoken The corse they follow did with desperate hand Fordo its own life. ’Twas of some estate. Couch we awhile and mark.

p.src: \[Retiring with Horatio.\]
LAERTES. What ceremony else?
HAMLET. That is Laertes, a very noble youth. Mark.

u.src: That is Laertes, a very noble youth.

p.src: LAERTES. What ceremony else?

PRIEST. Her obsequies have been as far enlarg’d As we have warranties. Her death was doubtful; And but that great command o’ersways the order, She should in ground unsanctified have lodg’d Till the last trumpet. For charitable prayers, Shards, flints, and pebbles should be thrown on her. Yet here she is allowed her virgin rites, Her maiden strewments, and the bringing home Of bell and burial.

p.src: LAERTES. Lay her i’ th’earth, And from her fair and unpolluted flesh May violets spring. I tell thee, churlish priest, A minist’ring angel shall my sister be When thou liest howling.

p.src: HAMLET. What, the fair Ophelia?
QUEEN. \[Scattering flowers.\] Sweets to the sweet. Farewell. I hop’d thou shouldst have been my Hamlet’s wife; I thought thy bride-bed to have deck’d, sweet maid, And not have strew’d thy grave.

p.src: LAERTES. O, treble woe Fall ten times treble on that cursed head Whose wicked deed thy most ingenious sense Depriv’d thee of. Hold off the earth a while, Till I have caught her once more in mine arms. \[Leaps into the grave.\] Now pile your dust upon the quick and dead, Till of this flat a mountain you have made, To o’ertop old Pelion or the skyish head Of blue Olympus.

p.src: HAMLET. \[Advancing.\] What is he whose grief Bears such an emphasis? whose phrase of sorrow Conjures the wand’ring stars, and makes them stand Like wonder-wounded hearers? This is I, Hamlet the Dane. \[Leaps into the grave.\]

p.src: HAMLET. Thou pray’st not well. I prithee take thy fingers from my throat; For though I am not splenative and rash, Yet have I in me something dangerous, Which let thy wiseness fear. Away thy hand!

QUEEN. Hamlet! Hamlet!
All. Gentlemen!
HORATIO. Good my lord, be quiet.

p.src: HAMLET. Why, I will fight with him upon this theme Until my eyelids will no longer wag.

u.src: Why, I will fight with him upon this theme Until my eyelids will no longer wag.

p.src: QUEEN. O my son, what theme?
HAMLET. I lov’d Ophelia; forty thousand brothers Could not, with all their quantity of love, Make up my sum. What wilt thou do for her?

p.src: KING. O, he is mad, Laertes.
QUEEN. For love of God forbear him!

u.src: For love of God forbear him!

p.src: HAMLET. ’Swounds, show me what thou’lt do: Woul’t weep? woul’t fight? woul’t fast? woul’t tear thyself? Woul’t drink up eisel? eat a crocodile? I’ll do’t. Dost thou come here to whine? To outface me with leaping in her grave? Be buried quick with her, and so will I. And if thou prate of mountains, let them throw Millions of acres on us, till our ground, Singeing his pate against the burning zone, Make Ossa like a wart. Nay, an thou’lt mouth, I’ll rant as well as thou.
